course_name_original: Métodos Numéricos en Sólidos y Fluidos (Ing. Gr.)
course_name_en: Numerical Methods in Solids and Fluids (Eng. Gr.)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the mathematical foundations of the Finite Volume Method (FVM) and the Finite Element Method (FEM).
Be able to implement and program numerical methods to solve simple engineering problems.
Be able to use commercial software that implements FVM and FEM.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical Modeling in Thermal and Fluid Engineering
Stationary Heat Conduction in Solids I. Orthogonal Meshes
Application of the Finite Volume Method (FVM)
Resolution of the Discrete Mathematical Model
Stationary Heat Conduction in Solids II. Non-Orthogonal Meshes
Heat Transfer in an Incompressible and Stationary Flow Fluid
First and Second Order Upwind Numerical Schemes
Incompressible and Stationary Flow of a Newtonian Fluid
Problem areas in the Numerical Resolution of the Navier-Stokes Equations
Numerical Scheme for Mass Flow Interpolation
Resolution of the Discrete Mathematical Model (DMM)
Introduction to the Finite Element Method (FEM)
Stiffness Matrix and Interpolation Functions in 1D elements
Displacement field, unit deformations and stresses
Displacement field, unit deformations and stresses
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes explaining the Finite Volume Method
Practical classes with guided exercises and time for assessed practices (for Fluid Dynamics)
Theoretical classes explaining the Finite Element Method
Practical classes with guided exercises and time for assessed practices (for Solids)
assessment_rules: To pass the course, both the Fluids and Solids parts must be passed. For the CFD part, each of the three multiple-choice tests requires a score over 3/10. For the Solids part, all practices and the 2D Elasticity project must be submitted, and both the theoretical and practical sections of the final exam require a score over 3/10. In the extraordinary examination, only the failed parts are re-evaluated for CFD, while for Solids, it consists of a 100% final exam (submission of previous practices is required), and the grades for approved parts are carried over.
